topic: The Geometric Relationship: Sphere Surface Area and Projected Shadow

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The Circle and the Sphere
sections.content: Briefly revisit the area of a circle (πr²) and define a sphere as a 3D set of points equidistant from a center. Introduce the visualization of a 'cross-section'—a flat slice through the center of a sphere results in a circle of the same radius.
sections.example: Visualizing an orange cut in half to reveal a perfect circular cross-section.

sections.title: The Geometry of the Projected Shadow
sections.content: Explain parallel projection: when a light source is at infinity (like the sun), a sphere casts a shadow on a perpendicular plane. The shadow is a circle with radius 'r'. State the key geometric fact: the area of this shadow is exactly πr².
sections.example: An animation showing a basketball blocking a flashlight, where the circular shadow matches the basketball's widest cross-section.

sections.title: Deriving the Sphere Surface Area
sections.content: Introduce Archimedes' Hat-Box Theorem: The surface area of a sphere is exactly 4 times the area of its projected shadow (or 4 times the area of its great circle). Formula: A = 4πr².
sections.example: A visual split-screen: The left side shows one circular shadow (πr²); the right side shows the sphere's surface 'unrolled' or tiled by four of those circular shadows.

sections.title: Practical Application: Calculating Solar Heat Gain
sections.content: Apply the concept to a real-world scenario. A satellite (spherical) receives sunlight. Only the 'shadow area' (πr²) intercepts the radiation, while the heat is distributed across the full surface area (4πr²).
sections.example: A space probe shaped like a sphere orbiting the sun; explaining why its temperature is determined by the ratio of the intercepting circle to the total radiating surface.

sections.title: Summary and Quick Check
sections.content: Recap: Shadow Area = πr², Surface Area = 4πr². Emphasize that the sphere's surface is 4 times the area of its shadow. Provide a quick mental calculation task.
sections.example: If a beach ball has a shadow of 1m², what is its total surface area? (Answer: 4m²).
